content:
There have been major problems with Spectrum/Charter/TWC/Roadrunner lately. Neither mail.twc.com (TWC's email servers) or mobile.charter.net (Spectrum and Charter's servers) appear to be online right now and may have been down for some time. From what we hear from their users, service has been intermittent for a while but it's gotten worse in the past week or few. It is not specifically a Thunderbird issue - it appears to affect most or all 3rd-party email clients, including Outlook, eMClient, etc. Spectrum's support usually (but not always!) won't admit to any problems, only saying that they only support webmail.

Here's a link to Spectrum's own user forum where you can see many discussions of the situation:

https://community.spectrum.net/categories/email-22

If you have time and patience you could contact Spectrum for status.

I have seen mention of a possible temporary workaround, which is to change the SMTP server to "mail.brighthouse.com". I can't verify that this works, or if it does that it won't quit working at any time, but it's easy enough to try and you can change it back to the existing name if it's not effective.

Otherwise, until they fix their servers your only recourse for now is to use their webmail. Or find another, more reliable email provider.

Yeah, Telstra are special. It said so on my front door when they came to visit to install a product they did not offer in my location. Excellent customer service. They have been experiencing higher than anticipate calls for 30 years I can remember ringing them and no one ever got fired.


I checked the setup database. It shows an IMAP option. It uses the same settings for bigpond.com, bigpond.net.au, telstra.com, bigpond.net, and Telstra,net See https://autoconfig.thunderbird.net/v1.1/bigpond.net

As Thunderbird always defaults to IMAP in the first instance we have an issue as to why you are not being offered to set it up. The only thing I can think of is you already have that account in Thunderbird (perhaps a failed attempt.) but I was wrong.

To try and understand I tried adding a fictitious email address at Bigpond. It would appear in their haste to get rid of the bigpond brand, they left the server settings on the web. Thunderbird is getting those POP settings directly from Telstra.

I assume the page you get looks like this

So I think the best way to fix this for now is create a broken account and then fix it after it is created.

So I tried creating bill@bigplod.com and I was offered IMAP.

On next I got

then I corrected the stuff I messed up as Thunderbird has done trying to get settings from telstra.

When I clicked on connect I was asked to correct the hostname. by clicking on the request I got this so I put in SMTP.telstra.com and told it to connect again.

Now my account simply does not exist so it had no hope of working out and I stopped there. But if you get that far and it is still complaining press the manual configuration and it will create the account and we can work on the why for the rest.

But I do have to ask you if you are sure you want to use IMAP and not POP. They are very different and you can not leave mails in your account long term as they consume space allocated for your account by telstra. POP only exist locally after it is downloads and the only space limitation is the size of your local hard disk. Having said that Telstra do allow you to store 10gb of email so you probably will not run out of space soon.
